data.problem: Understand OpenCode's plugin system (loading, hooks, auth integration, MCP support, config/secrets handling) well enough to reason about how to add or debug plugins and auth flows.
constraints: No code changes or implementation plans in explore phase
Prefer fastest path to learning and visible confirmation
Use existing repo artifacts and local configuration patterns

options.name: Inspect built-in plugin packages
options.approach: Locate the installed built-in plugin packages (opencode-anthropic-auth, opencode-gitlab-auth) and read their exports to confirm module format, auth hook usage, and any manifest conventions beyond the core SDK types.
options.what_we_learn: Real-world plugin module shape, auth hook patterns used outside core, and any implicit conventions not captured in types.

options.name: Run a minimal local plugin smoke test
options.approach: Create a minimal plugin in a .opencode/plugins directory, start OpenCode, and confirm load order, hook invocation, and tool registration behavior via logs or tool listing.
options.what_we_learn: Runtime behavior (installation, import, hook call order), and how plugin tooling behaves in practice.
options.risk_if_wrong: Low-to-medium; requires runtime setup and may hit local environment issues.

options.name: Exercise MCP auth flow end-to-end
options.approach: Configure a sample MCP remote server with OAuth, run the CLI auth flow, and verify storage/refresh behavior in mcp-auth.json and MCP status transitions.
options.what_we_learn: Practical MCP OAuth flow behavior, how tokens and client registrations are stored, and where failures surface.
options.risk_if_wrong: Medium; depends on an accessible MCP server and auth provider.

data.recommendation: Option 1 because it is the fastest confirmation of real plugin export/manifest conventions and auth patterns without needing runtime setup.
